subtitle: The architectural style behind Oracle Fusion's APIs

eyebrow: Three ideas make an API RESTful

steps.label: Resources
steps.sub: nouns like invoices or journals, each with its own URL

steps.label: Stateless
steps.sub: every request carries everything the server needs

steps.label: Standard verbs
steps.sub: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE — not custom action names

code:
GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoices
GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoices/300000182

Older style (not REST):
POST /getInvoiceById?id=300000182
caption: The invoice resource lives in the URL; the HTTP verb says what to do to it.

steps.label: Every call
steps.sub: carries its own credentials, every single time

steps.label: No session memory
steps.sub: Fusion's REST server recalls nothing from your last call

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.sub: any server in Oracle's pool can answer any request

subtitle: The verbs REST reuses, and what the server's answer means
